meta.name: Generate tailored resumes and cover letters with OpenRouter and Google Docs

name: Generate a tailored resume from a job posting in Google Docs

parameters.content:
### Heads up
LinkedIn often requires login to view full postings and may block anonymous scraping. if this returns a login page instead of the job description, use a company careers-page URL or Indeed instead.

If that still does not work, copy and paste the text inside job_text on the Extract Job Post Text node

## Generate a tailored resume from a job posting in Google Docs

### How it works

This workflow takes a job posting URL from a form, adds the candidate’s base profile details, and fetches the posting page. It extracts the job text and uses OpenRouter-powered AI steps to identify requirements, rewrite the resume, and draft a tailored cover letter. The generated resume and cover letter are combined into a new Google Doc, populated with the text, and moved into Google Drive.

### Setup steps

- Configure the form trigger so it captures the job posting URL field expected by the HTTP request node.
- Update the candidate profile/base resume Set node with the applicant’s name, contact details, portfolio URL, and resume source content.
- Add valid OpenRouter credentials for the extraction and writing language model nodes, and choose the desired models.
- Configure Google Docs and Google Drive credentials with permission to create, edit, and move documents.
- Set the destination Google Drive folder and verify the Google Docs nodes create and insert content into the intended document.

### Customization

Adjust the extraction prompt/schema to capture the job attributes you care about, such as required skills, seniority, keywords, company values, or salary details. You can also modify the resume and cover letter prompts to match a preferred tone, length, formatting style, or target role type.

## Collect candidate input

Starts the workflow from a submitted job posting URL and enriches the run with the candidate’s profile and base resume details.

## Fetch posting text

Retrieves the job posting web page and parses the HTML so the workflow can work with the posting’s readable text.

## Extract job requirements

Uses an information extraction step and its OpenRouter model to turn the parsed posting into structured job requirements for downstream generation.

## Generate tailored materials

Uses AI writing chains to rewrite the candidate’s resume for the extracted requirements and draft a matching cover letter, sharing the nearby OpenRouter writing model.

## Create application document

Combines the resume and cover letter outputs, creates a Google Doc, inserts the generated text, and moves the finished file in Google Drive.

nodes.name: Fetch Job Posting
nodes.notes: Some sites (LinkedIn especially) block anonymous scraping or require login and may return a login wall instead of the job text. If extraction comes back empty, paste the job description text directly into a modified version of this workflow instead of a URL.

nodes.name: AI Content Extractor
nodes.notes: Verify exact node type/params against your n8n instance (get_node_types) once MCP access is authorized — OpenRouter node params can drift between n8n versions.

messageValues.message:
=You are an expert resume writer and ATS optimization specialist. Rewrite the candidate's resume so it is precisely tailored to the target job, while staying 100% truthful to their actual experience — never invent employers, titles, dates, or accomplishments.

Tone: {{ $('Prepare Candidate Profile').item.json.tone }}
Language: {{ $('Prepare Candidate Profile').item.json.writing_language }}

Rules:
- Reorder and re-emphasize existing bullet points so the most relevant experience leads.
- Rewrite bullets to mirror the job's language and naturally include ATS keywords, without keyword-stuffing.
- Keep it to one page worth of content (roughly 500-650 words).
- Output clean plain text with clear section headers (SUMMARY, EXPERIENCE, SKILLS, EDUCATION), ready to paste into a document. No markdown symbols like ** or #.

=You are an expert career coach writing a compelling, specific, non-generic cover letter. Never use clichés like "I am excited to apply" or "I believe I would be a great fit" — open with a concrete hook tied to the company or role.

Tone: {{ $('Prepare Candidate Profile').item.json.tone }}
Language: {{ $('Prepare Candidate Profile').item.json.writing_language }}

Rules:
- 3-4 short paragraphs, under 350 words total.
- Paragraph 1: a specific hook — why this role/company, referencing something real about the company or role, not generic flattery.
- Paragraph 2-3: connect 2-3 real accomplishments from the resume directly to the job's key responsibilities, with concrete outcomes/numbers where the resume has them.
- Closing paragraph: confident call to action.
- Sign off with the candidate's name. Output clean plain text, no markdown symbols.

nodes.name: Generate Application Document
nodes.notes: folderId is set to Google Drive's 'root' alias (top level of My Drive). Open this node after import and pick a different folder from the dropdown if you want it saved elsewhere — the MCP can't resolve your real folder list without your live credential.
